source.title: Emergent Symbol-like Number Variables in Artificial Neural Networks
source.authors: Satchel Grant; Noah D. Goodman; James L. McClelland

record.tranche_reason: The study tests whether individual neuron activations can transfer a task-relevant count, and reports that direct neuron substitutions were relatively ineffective compared with interventions on neural subspaces.
record.gate_note: The study does not audit Qwen3-32B neuron poles or count interpretable neurons. Its result on individual neuron substitutions bears on V5. It also reports overlapping Phase and Count roles in raw neuron activity; that is recorded separately because it does not test attribution-graph sufficiency. Cited results from other studies are not included.
record.test_reason: The study does not test any version. It trains small GRUs, LSTMs and 2-layer transformers on synthetic counting tasks and aligns subspaces to symbolic algorithms with DAS. Its one neuron-level result is a patching test of two raw neurons in a 20-unit LSTM. That is not an attribution graph, not a large language model, and has no comparison with a replacement model or its reconstruction error, so it does not bear on V5. No neuron-pole audit, explanation-from-examples test, simulation scoring, InceptionV1 analysis or interpretable-share estimate is reported. Its neuron-versus-subspace argument is a related but different construct, so it goes under fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: Partly right but too narrow. The authors' main conclusions are threefold. RNNs develop graded, symbol-like Count and Phase variables, best found via causal interventions on neural subspaces rather than individual neurons. Linear alignment functions extend DAS where orthogonal alignments fail. Shallow transformers use anti-Markovian solutions, proven necessary without enough layers. The individual-neuron result is offered as a cautionary demonstration, not a main finding.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses DAS subspace interventions and direct individual-activation substitutions on synthetic number-task RNNs; it does not use the neuron-pole audit or attribution-graph method described in the claim.

fits_no_version.finding: In a 20-unit Multi-Object LSTM, patching two raw neurons highly correlated with Count (12 and 18) transferred Count with IIA 0.399. A 1-D linear-aligned subspace in the same model reached 82.6%.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In small recurrent networks on counting tasks, count-correlated individual neurons are causally insufficient to carry the task variable, while learned subspaces carry it far better.

fits_no_version.finding: Many raw neurons in the same LSTM contribute to both the aligned Phase and Count variables (visual, Fig. 4b).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In small RNNs, raw neurons participate in multiple task-variable representations (distributed coding).

record.problems: The neuron-substitution result is from a narrow synthetic task and a small LSTM (dm = 20); the reported IIA has no stated uncertainty or baseline, and the paper does not report separate values for neurons 12 and 18.
record.rows_left_out: No additional claim-relevant outcomes were reported that meet the row criteria.

untested.parts: No Qwen3-32B neuron-pole audit or job-count shares.
No language models, dense/MoE comparison or scale range.
No InceptionV1 or canonical polysemantic neuron reanalysis.
No interpretable-neuron shares across architectures, regularization or tools.
No attribution graphs, no large model, no replacement-model or reconstruction-error comparison.
No explanations from activating examples tested for predicting firing.
No simulation-based scoring of neuron explanations.

record.verdict_notes: The study does not cite or address the essay. The neurons-versus-subspaces theme is adjacent to the claim but is shown only in toy recurrent models, so no verdict is given. Relation 'discusses' is used loosely; T6 reflects that no version is tested or used.

versions.untested_parts: No audit of Qwen3-32B poles or their job counts.
No language-model, dense/MoE, or scale comparison.
No InceptionV1 examples or recursive-generalization analysis.
No estimates of interpretability shares across architectures or tools.

The study tests individual-neuron activation substitutions in a small recurrent model, not attribution graphs in a large model, full behavior explanation, or comparison with a trained replacement model and its reconstruction error.
No explanations written from activating examples or tests of their predictions on separate activations.
No automated scoring of neuron explanations on new text.

rows.subject: LSTM
rows.operation_detail: Directly substituted individual neuron activations from another sequence to transfer the Count; the paper highlights neurons 12 and 18.
rows.measure: Interchange Intervention Accuracy (IIA) for behavior expected from the Up-Down Count intervention
rows.note: The paper reports this result for substitutions involving neurons 12 and 18, without separate values for each. It also says the interventions produced no consistent behavioral pattern.
rows.check: Linked to V5 wrongly: a 20-unit LSTM on a synthetic counting task is not the large-model attribution-graph setting V5 names. The operation is also mis-described. Methods describe single-neuron substitutions for every neuron, but the reported IIA of 0.399 is for one joint intervention on neurons 12 and 18 together (§4.1.2). No per-neuron values are given. Baseline 'not stated' should note the comparison the paper draws: a 1-D LAF subspace in the same LSTM reached 82.6% Count IIA (Fig. 4 caption). With no version linked, no state against a version applies.

rows.subject: LSTM
rows.operation_detail: Visualized raw neuron activity and the inverse-projected aligned Phase and Count activity.
rows.measure: Whether raw neurons contribute to the aligned Phase and Count coding
rows.value: The authors state that many raw neurons can play a causal role in both Phase and Count coding.
rows.note: This is a visualization-based finding about overlapping roles in this model, not a test of attribution-graph sufficiency.
rows.check: Correctly unlinked. This is a qualitative visualization claim (Fig. 4b) with no numeric value; it concerns distributed coding in a tiny LSTM.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Highlighted individual-neuron substitutions in the Multi-Object LSTM
reader_labels.reason: Count transfer was incomplete (IIA 0.399), and the paper reports no consistent behavioral pattern; this qualifies claims that individual neurons suffice as analysis units in this setting (R1).
